literal.prompt: Как называют морской лёд, закреплённый у берега и не дрейфующий свободно?

literalGroups.primaryGround: WMO distinguishes fast ice (attached to shore or ocean floor) from drift ice (unattached) at L30. The competing labels denote distinct ice forms/stages: frazil crystals, nilas, and pancake disks (NSIDC L83-L88). Under the prompt’s attachment/no-drift definition, “припай” is the unique key.
literalGroups.locator: WMO turn2view2 L29-L30; NSIDC turn2view0 L83-L88.

literalGroups.literal: Это припай — морской лёд, прикреплённый к берегу или дну океана. Место прикрепления удерживает его от свободного дрейфа.
literalGroups.primaryGround: WMO defines fast ice as sea ice attached to shore or ocean floor, as distinct from drift ice unattached to either (L30).

literalGroups.literal: Игловидные кристаллы фразиля появляются при начале замерзания морской воды, всплывают и срастаются в ледяной лист.
literalGroups.primaryGround: NSIDC says small needle-like crystals called frazil form as ocean water begins to freeze, then float, accumulate and bond into sheets (L84). The note accurately teaches this early crystal stage, distinct from attached fast ice.

literalGroups.literal: Припай может прикрепляться не только к берегу, но и ко дну океана.
literalGroups.primaryGround: WMO identifies fast ice as sea ice attached to shore or ocean floor (L30); the prompt mentions shore only, so the note adds the supported alternate attachment to the ocean floor.

literalGroups.literal: Нилас — тонкая упругая сплошная корка морского льда.
literalGroups.primaryGround: NSIDC says grease ice develops into a continuous thin sheet called nilas (L85). WMO describes nilas as a thin elastic crust under 10 cm and treats young ice as a separate later 10–30 cm stage (L30); the new note avoids unsupported “young” and matte-surface claims.
literalGroups.locator: NSIDC turn2view0 L85; WMO turn2view2 L30.

literalGroups.literal: Блинчатый лёд образует округлые диски с приподнятыми краями, которые сталкиваются на волнах.
literalGroups.primaryGround: NSIDC describes pancake ice as rounded disks with raised perimeter edges produced when waves bump the disks together (L88). This is a distinct morphology, not shore/floor attachment.

fourFullPromptAnswerNoteAssessments.grammar: Natural Russian question and answer labels; all four options fit “как называют”, and each note is a grammatical declarative sentence.
fourFullPromptAnswerNoteAssessments.plausibilityUniqueKeyAndNoteTruthUsefuln: The Russian prompt is natural, and each noun label is grammatically suitable. “Припай” uniquely matches ice attached to shore and not freely drifting; frazil are initial crystals, nilas a thin sheet, and pancake ice round wave-raised disks.

correctNoteNewFact.newFact: Fast ice can attach to the ocean floor, in addition to the shore named by the prompt.
correctNoteNewFact.whyNew: The prompt and answer key state shore attachment/no free drift but not seabed attachment; this is a concrete additional property of the correct ice category.

entries.absoluteDifficulty: HARD fits a general adult audience because “при пай/fast ice” is specialized sea-ice classification by attachment and motion; the prompt tests a technical category and its distractors are neighboring types/stages, rather than broad everyday knowledge.
